home.title: ArtiFerris: a self-hosted npm and Docker registry in a single Rust binary
home.description: An npm registry and a Docker/OCI registry behind one console: hosted repositories, proxies and groups, quotas, retention, dependency audits, Trivy image scans and organizations by subdomain. One Rust binary and one PostgreSQL.

features.title: Product | ArtiFerris
features.description: What ArtiFerris does today: npm and Docker repositories, package pages, artifact analysis, organizations, a public catalog, mandatory two-factor authentication and administration. And what does not exist yet.

registries.title: npm and Docker registries | ArtiFerris
registries.description: npm, pnpm, yarn, docker and podman talk to ArtiFerris as they do to their usual registry. Hosted repositories, proxies in front of an upstream registry and groups behind a single address, with quotas and retention.

install.title: Installation | ArtiFerris
install.description: Install ArtiFerris with Docker Compose, with the Helm chart on Kubernetes or from source: commands, prerequisites and what happens on first start.

security.title: Security | ArtiFerris
security.description: Mandatory two-factor authentication, passwords hashed with Argon2, rights checked on every route, secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM, hashed tokens, audit and security logs, and data kept on your server.

roadmap.title: Roadmap | ArtiFerris
roadmap.description: Where ArtiFerris is heading: more package formats, object storage for several replicas, SAML, per-user namespaces and package provenance. None of this exists yet.

plan.title: Architecture of an ArtiFerris instance
plan.description: Isometric drawing. An npm or Docker client and a browser talk to a single Rust binary, artiferris-api, made of the crates api, npm, docker, application, domain and infrastructure. The binary keeps its data in PostgreSQL and its archives and blobs on disk, queries LDAP and OIDC directories and the SMTP server, and its proxies pull from upstream registries. An orange line follows an install to the upstream registry. Seven numbered circles lead to the tiles of the page.

package.title: A page per package
package.text: The README, sanitized on the server, the install command, the versions and tags, and the downloads of the last seven days.

scan.title: Every image is analyzed
scan.text: Trivy analyzes an image on every push, and the scan can be run again by hand. The dependencies of an npm package are audited on every publish.

search.title: A search that forgives typos
search.text: Packages, images and repositories, as you type. From three characters, a typo still finds the right package, ranked after the exact matches.

retention.title: Quota and retention
retention.text: A publish that would exceed the quota is refused. Retention keeps only the last N versions or tags; latest is never purged.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication, for everyone
mfa.text: No account can do without it: an authenticator app or a passkey, with ten backup codes. Accounts can also come from LDAP or OIDC.

regions.helm: Commands to install ArtiFerris on Kubernetes with Helm
regions.source: Commands to run ArtiFerris from its source code

notes.compose: Compose builds the image from source, Trivy included. Generate the secrets with `openssl rand -base64 48`, and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` with `openssl rand -hex 24`, since it ends up in a URL.
notes.helm: The chart generates the database password, `JWT_SECRET` and `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and finds them again from one deployment to the next. With `helm template`, Argo CD or Flux, set them yourself. The base domain is used for the organizations' subdomains.
notes.source: You need `rustup`, Node.js 26 and Docker with Compose. The script starts PostgreSQL, applies the migrations and runs the backend on port 8081 and the Angular development server on port 4200.

then.title: What happens next
then.secrets: The server refuses to start if `JWT_SECRET` or `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is shorter than 32 bytes or starts with `change-me`, if the first administrator's password is still the example one, or if `PUBLIC_URL` points to `0.0.0.0`.
then.start: It connects to PostgreSQL, applies its migrations, creates the first administrator if the users table is empty, and listens on port 8080.
then.signin: The first sign-in walks you through enrolling an authenticator app or a passkey, and shows your ten backup codes. There is no way around it.

needs.title: What you need
needs.docker: Docker with the Compose plugin, or a Kubernetes cluster with Traefik for the ingress.
needs.postgres: PostgreSQL 18: the Compose stack and the chart bring their own.
needs.storage: A persistent volume for the npm archives and the Docker blobs: storage is a local file system, served by a single replica.
needs.https: A domain name, a subdomain per organization, and TLS in front, through a reverse proxy. Passkeys only work on a secure origin.

hero.title: Your npm packages and Docker images, on a registry you host.
hero.subtitle: Hosted repositories, proxies and groups, quotas, retention, dependency audits and image scans: one Rust binary and one PostgreSQL. In production, the server and its database take about fifty MiB of memory together.
hero.assurance: No third-party account, no telemetry sent.

why.title: Use cases
why.text: Four typical situations, and how ArtiFerris answers them.

proxy.situation: Your builds download their dependencies from a public registry, every time.
proxy.answer: A proxy repository sits in front of `registry.npmjs.org` or Docker Hub: the first request fetches the package upstream, the next ones serve it from ArtiFerris. A group puts that proxy and your packages behind a single address.

tenants.situation: You host the packages of several teams or several customers on the same instance.
tenants.answer: Each organization has its subdomain, its repositories, its users, its branding and its identity provider. Its administrators act on it alone; a super-administrator sees them all.

scan.situation: You want to know what the images and packages you distribute contain.
scan.answer: Trivy analyzes every image pushed, and the scan can be run again by hand. The dependencies of an npm package are audited on every publish. The results show on the image or package page.

access.situation: You want two-factor authentication not to depend on everyone's diligence.
access.answer: It is mandatory for every account, whether local or coming from LDAP or OIDC. Command-line tools authenticate with an API token, which administration can list and revoke.

caps.title: Product overview
caps.text: Excerpts of the real interface, not mock-ups. The interface exists in French, English, Spanish, Italian and German.

registries.title: Two registries, one console
registries.text: ArtiFerris speaks the npm registry protocol and the Docker/OCI one: `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `docker` and `podman` use it as they would their usual registry. Each repository holds npm packages or Docker images, never both.

npm.title: One group, two members
npm.text: The `.npmrc` of a project points to a group. The group asks its members in the order you set, and the first one that holds the package answers. Turn the switch on to see what a second request changes.
npm.link: The npm registry in the documentation

docker.title: The Docker registry
docker.text: The password for `docker login` is an API token. Every push starts a Trivy scan of the image, whose results show on its page.
docker.link: The Docker registry in the documentation
docker.label: Log in, push and pull an image
docker.region: Docker commands for an organization repository

rules.title: The rules of a repository
rules.text: What each repository keeps, refuses and checks.

types.title: Three types of repository
types.text: Hosted for your own packages, proxy for a cache in front of an upstream registry, group for several repositories of the same format behind one address. Reading through a group takes `read` on each of its members.

quota.title: A quota per repository
quota.text: The room the repository may take. A publish that would exceed it is refused.

retention.title: Retention per repository
retention.text: Keep only the last N versions or tags. The purge runs every 6 hours, and `latest` is never purged. Republishing an unpublished npm version is refused.

audit.title: Dependencies audited
audit.text: On every publish, ArtiFerris audits the package's dependencies. `npm audit` also works against ArtiFerris; the audited names and versions are then sent to `registry.npmjs.org`.

scan.title: Images analyzed
scan.text: Trivy, shipped in the ArtiFerris image, analyzes every image pushed. A scan can be run again by hand from the image page.

public.title: Public repositories
public.text: A public repository can be read without an account and shows in the public catalog. Anonymous reads have a budget per client and per minute, 1,200 by default.

install.title: Installation
install.text: ArtiFerris fits in one container image: the server, both registries, the interface and Trivy. It needs PostgreSQL and a volume. Three ways to install it: Docker Compose, the Helm chart on Kubernetes, or from source.

made.title: Architecture
made.text: One process, six crates, a hexagonal architecture: the domain knows nothing of the database, and each registry protocol has its own crate.

crates.domain: Entities, value objects and the ports the rest depends on. No input or output.
crates.application: The use cases. Depends on the domain only.
crates.infrastructure: Adapters: PostgreSQL (SQLx), files, SMTP, LDAP, OIDC, Trivy, Argon2, JWT.
crates.api: The Axum server: routes, wiring, and the Angular front end. It is the binary.

security.title: Security and your data
security.text: The measures that protect an instance, described precisely. The data stays on your server; only the names and versions of audited packages go to registry.npmjs.org.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication is mandatory
mfa.text: An authenticator app or a passkey, with ten backup codes. A separate, short-lived token stands for "password checked, second factor expected"; it does not act as a session.

passwords.title: Passwords hashed with Argon2
passwords.text: For local accounts. LDAP and OIDC accounts authenticate with their provider, and failed sign-ins are throttled.

rights.title: Rights checked on every route
rights.text: A repository's rights are enforced by the server, not just hidden in the interface. Request bodies are only read after these checks.

secrets.title: Secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM
secrets.text: SMTP, LDAP and OIDC passwords, proxy credentials and TOTP seeds, under `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which can be changed without loss through a rotation.

tokens.title: Tokens, stored hashed
tokens.text: Command-line tools authenticate with an API token, which the server cannot read back. The tokens Docker gets after `docker login` last 2 minutes.

bodies.title: Bounded memory
bodies.text: Docker blobs go to disk as they arrive. Documents kept in memory draw on a 1 GiB budget, and a client has at most four bodies in progress.

anonymous.title: A budget for anonymous traffic
anonymous.text: Public pages, the public API and npm and Docker reads have a budget per client and per minute, shared between replicas. The database only receives fingerprints, never an address.

audit.title: Audit and security logs
audit.text: Kept 365 days by default. Sign-ins, denied accesses and administrative actions are recorded there.

outbound.title: Controlled outbound connections
outbound.text: LDAP, SMTP, OIDC and proxies reach no private address, except the ranges you allow. A proxy only sends its credentials to the configured upstream registry, over `https`.

data.title: Your data, on your server
data.text: PostgreSQL and a volume, both yours to back up. With the Helm chart, the pod runs unprivileged, on a read-only file system.

security.link: The Security section of the README

headers.label: Headers of an ArtiFerris response
headers.caption: The production instance, version 0.6.1, asked for /healthz on 6 October 2026. The server sets the content policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and the Cross-Origin policies; here, Strict-Transport-Security and X-XSS-Protection come from the reverse proxy.

storage.text: Storage is a local file system: one volume, one replica. S3-compatible storage is planned.

saml.title: No SAML
saml.text: Accounts come from ArtiFerris, from LDAP or Active Directory, or from an OIDC provider.

provenance.title: No package signing

features.title: What ArtiFerris does today
features.intro: Everything on this page exists today. What is planned is in the roadmap.
features.note: The application's interface exists in five languages; its documentation is in French.

repos.title: Repositories
repos.text: npm and Docker repositories, filed by organization or under your own name.

bullets.b1: Three types per format: hosted, proxy in front of an upstream registry, and group of several repositories behind one address
bullets.b2: `read`, `write` and `admin` rights, granted user by user
bullets.b3: A storage quota and a retention per repository; `latest` is never purged
bullets.b4: Public repositories, readable without an account, or private ones

packages.text: A page per npm package and per Docker image.

bullets.b1: npm: publish, install, unpublish and dist-tags, with `npm`, `pnpm` or `yarn`
bullets.b2: Docker/OCI: push, pull and manifest deletion, with `docker` or `podman`
bullets.b3: The README of an npm package, converted and sanitized on the server, and its install command
bullets.b4: The size of each tag of an image, and the downloads of the last seven days
bullets.b5: Republishing an unpublished npm version is refused

scan.title: Artifact analysis
scan.text: What the packages and images you distribute contain.

bullets.b1: Dependency audit of an npm package on every publish
bullets.b2: A Trivy scan of every Docker image pushed, which can be run again by hand
bullets.b3: The results on the package or image page, with their severity

tenants.title: Organizations
tenants.text: Several teams or several customers on the same instance.

bullets.b1: One organization per subdomain, with its repositories and users

bullets.b1: A catalog per format, a search that forgives typos and suggestions as you type
bullets.b2: The `/@user` and `/o/organization` profiles, and the page of each public package
bullets.b3: Search engine indexing, off by default and adjustable per organization

bullets.b1: Open to everyone, signed in or not
bullets.b2: Getting started, usage (repositories, npm, Docker, account and tokens, public catalog), administration and the public API

bullets.b1: Mandatory for every account: an authenticator app (TOTP) or a passkey, and backup codes
bullets.b2: Local accounts, LDAP or Active Directory, and OIDC
bullets.b3: Invitations by e-mail: the administrator only enters the address, the invitee chooses their username
bullets.b4: Personal API tokens, which administrators can list and revoke

bullets.b1: A dashboard, usage metrics and a health page
bullets.b2: An audit log and a security log
bullets.b3: Users, resetting their password or their two-factor authentication, and SMTP with a test e-mail
bullets.b4: Export and import of the configuration

bullets.b1: French, English, Spanish, Italian and German; the account's language comes before the browser's
bullets.b2: E-mails and the titles of public pages follow the reader's language

tech.title: Technical aspects
tech.text: What you deploy and what it needs.

bullets.b1: A single Rust binary (Axum) serves the API, both registries and the Angular web application
bullets.b2: PostgreSQL 18 for the data; archives and blobs on a volume
bullets.b3: Docker Compose or a Helm chart for Kubernetes; image `masmarino/artiferris`, Trivy included
bullets.b4: A hexagonal architecture, split over six Cargo crates

ferrisgit.title: The link with FerrisGit
ferrisgit.text: FerrisGit, the Git forge of the same family, plans to publish an artifact built by a pipeline to ArtiFerris, to trace each artifact back to the commit that produced it, and to bring ArtiFerris's analysis results into the checks of its merge requests. An identity shared between the two remains an open question.
